messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High packet loss detected from CDN POP eu-central-3 -> origin (avg 18% over 3m). Potential customer impact: increased tail latency and failed websocket connections. Incident INC-2026-458 created. @luca oncall page.

luca: got the page, investigating. seeing spike in 4xx/5xx from eu-central-3 POP in the dashboard. attaching quick graph: https://console.redwood/infr/graphs/INC-2026-458

luca: initial checks: provider status shows no broad AZ outage, but BGP peers for pop-eu-central-3 show intermittent flaps. traceroute from edge to origin: ```traceroute to origin.redwood.internal (10.20.30.40), 30 hops max 1 10.0.0.1 1.2 ms 2 172.16.0.5 2.3 ms 3 * * * 4 192.0.2.1 28.9 ms 5 10.20.30.40 29.4 ms``` some hops dropping packets.

luca: mitigation idea: enable POP-fallback routing for eu-central traffic to eu-west-1 (soft-failover) and temporarily increase max request timeout for streaming calls. gonna try reroute policy if net team ok.

maya: thanks @luca. I'm net-ops. currently seeing 20-25% packet loss at peering links for pop-eu-central-3 -> transit-ASN 64555. Provider acknowledges degraded egress to certain ISPs, working with upstream. Policy-wise we can shift BGP local-preference for customer prefixes to use eu-west-1 POP within 90s. Prepare a rollback plan.

luca: will apply routing policy now. tagging @jamie for SRE involvement and @rosa for support comms (customer impact).

jamie: on it. I'll watch service-level errors and spin up temporary extra capacity in eu-west-1 to handle rerouted traffic. also enabling token-cache warmups to reduce cold-start failures.

luca: running apply: ```redwoodctl routing set-pop-preference --from eu-central-1 --to eu-west-1 --prefixes service/* --weight 90 --dry-run=false```

sim: net-ops-bot: BGP-change queued. Change ID BGPC-778 applied to edge routers for pop-eu-central-3. Propagation started.

maya: change is visible in provider console. telemetry shows drop in packet loss from 22% -> 6% for rerouted prefixes in the last minute.

rosa: support note: initial customer triage — approx 12 accounts with elevated error rates, most sessions recover after retry. ETA for status update to customers: 20 minutes. Drafting message in #support-updates.

anna: engineering note: for customers hitting model timeouts, enable fallback to smaller model (latency-first) per-route: ```routes: - match: /api/v1/generate action: fallback_model: rwd-mini-1``` Doing a canary on 10% first.

luca: oncall handoff in 30m — @maya will take lead after that. recording actions and runbook in the incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/INC-2026-458

maya: acknowledged. I'll pick up the oncall at 1782003000. Current status: partial mitigation via POP-fallback, customer impact reduced to intermittent latency spikes and retries. Provider follow-up required for full resolution.

jamie: monitoring logs: error-rate down from 7% -> 1.2% for affected endpoints. no data loss reported. continuing to monitor for 45 mins before full rollback of temporary routing.

rosa: sent first customer status update. customers asked for ETA; told them provider investigating and we've applied safe failover.

sim: net-ops-bot: Provider ticket UP-908 updated: "Investigating egress peering issue; suspected ISP hardware flapping. Estimated fix 2-4h."

maya: action items for handoff -> @maya (net-ops), @jamie (sre), @rosa (support): 1) monitor metrics and keep support updates every 30m; 2) keep BGP fallback in place until provider confirms stable; 3) prepare rollback plan once provider confirms; 4) update incident doc and postmortem stub.

luca: handing off to @maya now. leaving notes in thread. thanks team. :thumbsup:

maya: taking lead. will post interim summary at +30 and update last_message_ts when we close.

jamie: adding one more: enable additional logs on streaming layer for 1h to capture any residual partial TCP resets. ```telemetryctl stream-logs --service streaming --duration 1h --label incident=INC-2026-458```

rosa: next customer update posted. support queue reduced. closing escalation to oncall after handoff.

maya: INTERIM SUMMARY (auto): incident INC-2026-458: pop eu-central-3 experienced upstream peering packet loss causing increased errors/latency for subset of customers. Temporary POP -> eu-west-1 routing applied; error-rate reduced from peak ~22% packet loss to ~1-2% service errors. Oncall: maya (lead), jamie (SRE), rosa (support). Provider ticket UP-908 open.

maya: marking incident as mitigated for production traffic at 1782002000. will keep monitoring until provider resolves. follow-up: postmortem and root cause to be authored by net-ops + SRE.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-458 status updated: mitigated. Timeline and actions captured.

maya: thanks all. closing thread for active paging. if we see re-escalation, reopen."
